notes: Cross-verse consistency (rule 24). The chapter renders a substantival article whose complement is a predicate adjective three times — 16.10, 16.12, 16.15 — and analysed 16.10 differently from the other two, giving the article a bare pronoun and the relativizer to the adjective, where 16.12 and 16.15 give the article the antecedent and the relativizer together. Nothing in the source licenses the difference: all three are article + adjective, and only the English free-relative idiom differs ('He that ...' against 'that which ...'). Rule 22 lists τῷ -> 'that which' on the article as the canonical reading, which is 16.12's own construction, and rule 32 confines the pronoun-only split to a participle because a participle has a verb of its own to carry the relativizer. An adjective has none, so rule 31's verbless-modifier reasoning applies and the article keeps the relativizer while the adjective keeps only the supplied copula and its own word. Both halves of the verse are corrected the same way.
